items.title: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Sol and Luna
items.oneliner: OpenAI priced GPT-6 Sol at $2/$10 and Luna at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens, forcing a real model price war.

items.title: Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5.5
items.oneliner: Anthropic says Opus 5.5 cuts typical workload cost 40%, signaling frontier gains now come with hard pricing pressure.

items.title: China leads open-weight model momentum
items.oneliner: Chinese labs now lead open-weight releases, shifting the practical open model center of gravity away from US incumbents.

items.title: WordPress fixed a critical RCE path
items.oneliner: WordPress patched a 9.2 CVSS unauthenticated traversal bug that can become RCE, so lagging updates are now indefensible.

items.title: GitHub Actions caches can leak secrets
items.oneliner: Rust warned that Miri output cached in GitHub Actions can expose secrets to pull requests through the target directory.

items.title: A BGP hijack pushed malicious updates
items.oneliner: Attackers paired a BGP hijack with a valid TLS certificate to deliver malicious Softaculous updates, which is nightmare-grade supply chain abuse.

items.title: Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent
items.oneliner: Amazon blocked Meta's Muse after reports it referenced private messages, showing agent distribution will hinge on trust, not demos.

items.title: Intel NPUs can run custom kernels
items.oneliner: Npunlock gets custom C kernels running on Intel NPUs, turning locked laptop silicon into something developers can actually program.

items.title: Agent harnesses are becoming products
items.oneliner: Unreal Agent claims up to 40% lower production cost than Codex, making the harness itself a serious optimization layer.

items.title: Tokens are becoming infrastructure pricing
items.oneliner: If tokens keep collapsing in price, model choice becomes an infrastructure decision, not a premium software subscription.
